![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/36ea34524b2ca277e8061441492711d36c8065e765d519d85d4008da97c3f8b3.png)

Consider the figure shown above. Which of the following triplets of points are collinear?

I. $M,N,R$

II. $P,S,T$

III. $O,P,S$
question.worked_solution:
- $M,N,R$ are collinear since there is a straight line that passes through all of them.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/b8fae613772422b14fce2e2db0762f659599f0b17409223ec291802b5d760d9c.png)

- $P,S,T$ are **not** collinear since we can't draw a straight line that passes through all of them.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/85638c1466360f3e5285c34e84903824140b9e2fc72a0f029ab1ded170b64eb2.png)

- $O,P,S$ are collinear since there is a straight line that passes through all of them.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/4b7ef30e306e3c7e70dadb1524e1f60a9ea01832215009ef2ea8344cb07e7297.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
